note: Short answers are graded against stated exact values. Immediate practice, repeated questions and reported assistance stay separate from delayed checks with an unseen question. These limited checks do not certify expertise or change mastery.

concepts.title: Run Python in your own workspace

questions.prompt: Your project uses .venv/bin/python. Complete the package-install command with the interpreter path: ____ -m pip install pytest. Type only the path.
questions.explanation: Run pip through the same interpreter that runs the project. A different pip may install into another environment.

questions.prompt: A program reports the interpreter it is actually using. Complete this Python expression with the attribute name: sys.____. Type only the attribute.
questions.explanation: sys.executable shows the current interpreter path. Compare it with the interpreter selected by your editor.

questions.prompt: What does this print? Type the number without quotes.
questions.explanation: Both operands are text, so + joins them. Convert validated numeric text before doing arithmetic.

questions.prompt: This function must preserve an explicit zero. What does this print? Type the number.
questions.explanation: Use is None when only None means missing. Zero is a real value here.
questions.code:
limit = 0
value = 90 if limit is None else limit
print(value)
questions.validation:
limit = 0
value = 90 if limit is None else limit
print(value)

questions.prompt: What does this print? Type the lowercase word, without quotes.
questions.explanation: String methods return new strings. The cleaned value changes; the original name still points to its old string.
questions.code:
title = " BOOK "
cleaned = title.strip().lower()
print(cleaned)
questions.validation:
title = " BOOK "
cleaned = title.strip().lower()
print(cleaned)

questions.prompt: What number is printed?
questions.explanation: The list keeps all three rows. A set would remove the duplicate tea entry.
questions.code:
rows = ["tea", "tea", "fruit"]
print(len(rows))
questions.validation:
rows = ["tea", "tea", "fruit"]
print(len(rows))

questions.prompt: What number is printed?
questions.explanation: The dictionary is created once before the loop, so each row adds to the existing total.

questions.prompt: What number is printed?
questions.explanation: The loop has no items. Keeping an initial total of zero gives a valid result for empty input.
questions.code:
total = 0
for amount in []:
    total += amount
print(total)
questions.validation:
total = 0
for amount in []:
    total += amount
print(total)

questions.prompt: What does the final print call output? Type the Python value without quotes.
questions.explanation: A function without a return statement returns None. Printing inside it would not return its text either.

questions.prompt: A money parser accepts at most two decimal digits. It receives "9.876". Which exception does the stated contract require? Type its Python class name.
questions.explanation: The value violates the contract. Reject it with ValueError rather than silently rounding or cutting digits.

questions.prompt: The file path exists in the request, but the file is missing. Type the specific built-in exception name used for this case.
questions.explanation: Catch the expected file error at the file boundary. Catching every Exception can hide unrelated bugs.

questions.prompt: What does the last print call output? Type the exception class name.
questions.explanation: The original exception still travels to the caller. A useful boundary can add context while keeping the cause.

questions.prompt: Which standard-library module reads a quoted comma as part of one CSV field? Type the module name.
questions.explanation: csv.reader understands quoting. Splitting each line on commas would split the field itself.

questions.prompt: A CLI contract requires either a complete report or an error. It has read four valid rows, but validation is not finished. Should it print the report yet? Type yes or no.
questions.explanation: Wait until all rows validate. Otherwise later failure leaves a partial report that looks successful.

questions.prompt: What string is assigned to __name__ when this file runs directly as a Python script? Type it without quotes.
questions.explanation: The __main__ guard runs the command only when the file is executed directly, so importing it does not start the CLI.

questions.prompt: This CLI contract uses status 0 for success and status 1 for a missing input file. The requested file is absent. Type the required status number.
questions.explanation: A nonzero exit status tells calling scripts that the command failed. Send the error text to stderr.

concepts.title: Test and build your expense tracker

questions.prompt: What number does the second call print?
questions.explanation: The default list is shared between calls. A regression test with two calls exposes the accumulated state.

questions.prompt: A test mocks parse_amount itself and asserts that the mock returns its configured value. Did this test check the real parser? Type yes or no.
questions.explanation: The test only checked the replacement. Call the real parser to check its behavior; fake external dependencies when needed.

questions.prompt: How many bytes does this UTF-8 encoding contain? Type the number.
questions.explanation: The Python string has one character here, but UTF-8 uses two bytes for that character.
questions.code: print(len("é".encode("utf-8")))
questions.validation: print(len("é".encode("utf-8")))

questions.prompt: What exception class does strict UTF-8 decoding raise for b"\xff"? Type its name.
questions.explanation: Invalid UTF-8 cannot be decoded exactly. Strict decoding reports the error rather than quietly dropping bytes.

questions.prompt: What number is printed?
questions.explanation: A dictionary stores one value per key. The second write replaces the first event at that key.
questions.code:
events = {}
events[12] = "opened"
events[12] = "closed"
print(len(events))
questions.validation:
events = {}
events[12] = "opened"
events[12] = "closed"
print(len(events))

questions.prompt: Consuming zip([1, 2], [3], strict=True) detects unequal lengths. Type the exception class name.
questions.explanation: strict=True reports a length mismatch. Ordinary zip stops at the shorter input and can hide missing data.

questions.prompt: What date is printed? Type YYYY-MM-DD.
questions.explanation: timedelta handles month boundaries. The day after February 29 in a leap year is March 1.
questions.code:
from datetime import date, timedelta
print(date(2024, 2, 29) + timedelta(days=1))
questions.validation:
from datetime import date, timedelta
print(date(2024, 2, 29) + timedelta(days=1))

questions.prompt: An event contract requires a UTC offset. This timestamp has none: 2026-04-08T10:30:00. Should the parser accept it under that contract? Type yes or no.
questions.explanation: A time without an offset does not identify a unique instant. The contract requires rejecting it rather than guessing a zone.

questions.prompt: A timestamp is 18:00 at UTC+05:00. What UTC time represents the same instant? Type HH:MM.
questions.explanation: Subtract the five-hour offset. Converting the zone preserves the instant; relabeling tzinfo would change it.

questions.prompt: Which time-module clock is used to measure elapsed work without relying on wall-clock adjustments? Type the function name, without parentheses.
questions.explanation: time.perf_counter is suited to elapsed measurements. time.monotonic is also monotonic; use the difference between two readings.

questions.prompt: What does repr reveal as the final escaped character in this string? Type only the two-character escape, including its backslash.
questions.explanation: repr makes the newline visible. Looking at plain printed text can hide the character that caused the mismatch.
questions.code:
text = "ready\n"
print(repr(text))

questions.prompt: A reported bug is fixed. A new test recreates the old failure and fails when the fix is removed. Is that a regression test? Type yes or no.
questions.explanation: The test preserves the failure as repeatable evidence and helps stop the same bug from returning.

questions.prompt: What number is printed?
questions.explanation: A shallow copy still shares the nested list. Mutating through the copy changes the original list too.
questions.code:
original = {"values": []}
copy = original.copy()
copy["values"].append(9)
print(original["values"][0])
questions.validation:
original = {"values": []}
copy = original.copy()
copy["values"].append(9)
print(original["values"][0])

questions.prompt: What number does the second call print?
questions.explanation: None is replaced with a fresh list inside each call, so the calls do not share their results.

questions.prompt: What number is printed?
questions.explanation: The list belongs to the class and both instances refer to it. Put per-instance mutable state in __init__.
questions.code:
class Inbox:
    titles = []

a = Inbox()
b = Inbox()
a.titles.append("read")
print(len(b.titles))
questions.validation:
class Inbox:
    titles = []

a = Inbox()
b = Inbox()
a.titles.append("read")
print(len(b.titles))

questions.prompt: An inbox count should always reflect len(self.titles). Complete the decorator name for a read-only computed attribute: @____. Type the name.
questions.explanation: A property computes the count from current state. A separate stored count can drift when the list changes.

questions.prompt: What number is printed?
questions.explanation: frozen=True stops assigning attributes. It does not make the list inside the object immutable.
questions.code:
from dataclasses import dataclass
@dataclass(frozen=True)
class Item:
    tags: list[str]

item = Item([])
item.tags.append("new")
print(len(item.tags))
questions.validation:
from dataclasses import dataclass
@dataclass(frozen=True)
class Item:
    tags: list[str]

item = Item([])
item.tags.append("new")
print(len(item.tags))

questions.prompt: Complete this dataclass declaration for a fresh list per instance: labels: list[str] = field(____=list). Type the keyword.
questions.explanation: The factory builds a new list for each instance. One shared mutable default would mix their state.

questions.prompt: A service rejects a blank title, but it currently saves the record first. Which step must come first: validation or storage? Type one word.
questions.explanation: Validate before changing state. Otherwise a rejected request can leave a saved record behind.

questions.prompt: A task service receives a store object and delegates saving to it. Is this composition or inheritance? Type one word.
questions.explanation: The service uses a store; it is not a kind of store. Supplying the store lets tests replace that dependency.

questions.prompt: What type name is printed?
questions.explanation: Annotations do not convert or validate values at runtime. A request boundary must check the actual value.

questions.prompt: A function returns str | None. What singleton should you check for before calling .upper() on the result? Type its Python name.
questions.explanation: None has no .upper() method. Handle the empty-result case before using string methods.

concepts.title: Protocols, fakes & the typed task inbox

questions.prompt: A type checker accepts a store with the required compatible methods even though it does not inherit the protocol. Type the typing class name that describes this contract.
questions.explanation: A Protocol describes the needed shape. Compatible implementations can satisfy it without inheritance.

questions.prompt: A validation test uses the real task service and a fake store that records writes. Invalid input is submitted. How many writes should the fake record under the contract? Type the number.
questions.explanation: The real service must reject the input before calling storage. A recording fake makes accidental writes visible.

questions.prompt: What does the final print output? Type the empty Python collection exactly.
questions.explanation: The iterator has already been consumed. A second pass does not restart it.
questions.code:
cursor = iter([4, 5])
list(cursor)
print(list(cursor))
questions.validation:
cursor = iter([4, 5])
list(cursor)
print(list(cursor))

questions.prompt: Which built-in exception signals that next(iterator) has no more items? Type its class name.
questions.explanation: next raises StopIteration at exhaustion. A for loop handles that signal for you.

questions.prompt: What number is printed?
questions.explanation: Creating a generator does not run its body. The append happens when the caller advances it.
questions.code:
seen = []
def source():
    seen.append(1)
    yield 1

iterator = source()
print(len(seen))
questions.validation:
seen = []
def source():
    seen.append(1)
    yield 1

iterator = source()
print(len(seen))

questions.prompt: What number is printed?
questions.explanation: The first next call advances only far enough to reach the first yield. It has not consumed the second item.
questions.code:
seen = []
def source():
    for value in [7, 8]:
        seen.append(value)
        yield value

iterator = source()
next(iterator)
print(len(seen))
questions.validation:
seen = []
def source():
    for value in [7, 8]:
        seen.append(value)
        yield value

iterator = source()
next(iterator)
print(len(seen))

questions.prompt: A generator is passed to sorted(source). Must sorting collect its items before returning the sorted list? Type yes or no.
questions.explanation: sorted consumes the input and builds a list. A lazy source does not make this consumer use bounded memory.

questions.prompt: A line reader has a byte limit of 4096. It reads at most limit + 1 bytes so it can detect overflow. Type the maximum number of bytes read in that probe.
questions.explanation: The extra byte tells you whether the line exceeds the limit without first loading an arbitrarily large line.

questions.prompt: What type name is printed?
questions.explanation: raise ... from error keeps the original exception in __cause__, so callers can inspect both layers.

questions.prompt: What does this print?
questions.explanation: Returning from finally replaces the pending exception. Cleanup should avoid returning a success value that hides failure.

concepts.title: Context managers & the streaming log lab

questions.prompt: What boolean does the final print output? Type True or False.
questions.explanation: Leaving the with block closes the owned stream even when the body raises.
questions.code:
from io import StringIO
stream = StringIO("data")
try:
    with stream:
        raise ValueError("stop")
except ValueError:
    pass
print(stream.closed)
questions.validation:
from io import StringIO
stream = StringIO("data")
try:
    with stream:
        raise ValueError("stop")
except ValueError:
    pass
print(stream.closed)

questions.prompt: A helper borrows an open stream from its caller. The stated contract leaves stream ownership with the caller. Should the helper close it after reading? Type yes or no.
questions.explanation: Borrowing access does not transfer ownership. The caller decides when its stream closes.

questions.prompt: A conditional reservation update requires available > 0. It returns no rows because available is 0. How many orders may this transaction create under the reservation contract? Type the number.
questions.explanation: No returned row means the reservation failed. Do not create an order without a successful reservation in the same transaction.

questions.prompt: Transaction A locks rows 1 then 2; B locks 2 then 1. What failure can their opposite lock order cause? Type the single database term.
questions.explanation: Each transaction can wait for a row held by the other. Use a consistent lock order and retry the whole aborted transaction.

questions.prompt: A documented API contract returns HTTP 409 when an idempotency key is reused with a different request body. A caller does exactly that. Type the status number.
questions.explanation: The same operation key must not authorize a different payload. Return the documented conflict rather than silently performing new work.

questions.prompt: A client retries a payment after a lost response. Its operation key was pay-73. Type the key that the retry must preserve.
questions.explanation: Keep the identity of the original intended payment. A new key could create a second payment.

concepts.title: The crash between commit and ack

questions.prompt: A worker commits a ledger change, then crashes before broker acknowledgement. Can an at-least-once broker deliver the event again? Type yes or no.
questions.explanation: The broker still sees unacknowledged work. Make the repeated business effect safe with a stable event identity.

questions.prompt: The consumed-event marker and its ledger mutation must succeed or fail together. Type the database boundary that should contain both: one ____.
questions.explanation: Committing the marker separately can mark unfinished work as consumed. Keep it in the same transaction as the effect.

questions.prompt: An order and its publication intent need one atomic database commit. Type the table-pattern name that stores the pending event intent.
questions.explanation: Write the order and the outbox row in the same transaction. A relay can publish that durable intent later.

questions.prompt: An outbox relay published an event and crashed before recording sent. Can its retry publish a duplicate? Type yes or no.
questions.explanation: The outbox protects publication intent, but publishing and marking sent are separate operations. Consumers still need idempotency.

questions.prompt: An async route directly calls a blocking HTTP client. Does the async keyword alone make that call nonblocking? Type yes or no.
questions.explanation: The blocking call still blocks the event loop. Use an appropriate synchronous route or a consistently async client and stack.

questions.prompt: Three repository operations belong to one all-or-error use case. How many success commits should that use case perform? Type the number.
questions.explanation: One transaction boundary keeps the use case atomic. Helpers may flush, but independent commits can leave partial success.

concepts.title: A queue is a failure boundary

questions.prompt: A malformed event fails the same way on every retry. Can unbounded retries repair its invalid data? Type yes or no.
questions.explanation: Retry cannot repair a permanent input error. Bound attempts, quarantine the event and preserve diagnostic evidence.

questions.prompt: A paused worker resumes after its lock lease expired and another worker took over. Is its old lease proof that it may still write? Type yes or no.
questions.explanation: The old holder can resume late. Use storage-enforced fencing or another invariant that rejects stale work.

questions.prompt: A server inside a container must listen on all IPv4 interfaces so another service can reach it. Type the bind address.
questions.explanation: Container loopback is private to that container. Binding all interfaces permits service networking; published host ports are a separate choice.

questions.prompt: Old replicas still read a column. Is dropping it immediately during a mixed-version rollout compatible? Type yes or no.
questions.explanation: Use an expand/migrate/contract sequence so both old and new replicas work during the rollout.

concepts.title: A model response is a proposal

questions.prompt: An expense is schema-valid but names another tenant's account. Does valid JSON authorize the expense? Type yes or no.
questions.explanation: Shape validation does not establish ownership. The application must authorize the operation using the authenticated principal.

questions.prompt: A model runs at temperature zero. Does that setting prove that its answers are correct? Type yes or no.
questions.explanation: Sampling settings do not prove truth, authorization or stable behavior across model and system changes.

questions.prompt: A reranker receives 30 candidates. The correct document is absent from all 30. Can reranking only those candidates recover it? Type yes or no.
questions.explanation: A reranker can reorder its input but cannot recover a document that retrieval did not supply.

questions.prompt: Two embedding models produce vectors of the same size. Does equal size alone make their vectors directly comparable? Type yes or no.
questions.explanation: Different models can learn different spaces. Keep model/version metadata and use the matching query encoder.

questions.prompt: The right passage is in the final context, but the answer contradicts it. Which stage should be investigated first: retrieval or generation? Type one word.
questions.explanation: Retrieval already supplied the evidence. Inspect generation instructions, model behavior and support checks at this boundary.

questions.prompt: Tenant filtering is correct, but the final-answer cache uses only question text. Can that cache still leak another tenant's answer? Type yes or no.
questions.explanation: Cached answers also need authorization scope. Filtering retrieval does not protect an unsafe answer cache.

questions.prompt: A model supplies role=admin in tool arguments. Is that trusted evidence of the caller's privileges? Type yes or no.
questions.explanation: The service derives authority from the authenticated principal and applies permissions outside model output.

questions.prompt: An approved transfer names account A. A later proposed transfer changes the recipient to account B. Does the old approval automatically cover the changed action? Type yes or no.
questions.explanation: Approval belongs to a concrete identity and parameters. Changing the recipient requires authorization for that changed action.

concepts.title: A prompt change is a release

questions.prompt: A candidate raises the average quality score but introduces a cross-tenant leak. May it pass a release gate that requires zero such leaks? Type yes or no.
questions.explanation: An average improvement cannot override a failed security gate. Report the failure and keep the candidate out of that release.

questions.prompt: A benchmark was used for every prompt adjustment. Is it still an untouched held-out evaluation set? Type yes or no.
questions.explanation: Tuning against the benchmark turns it into development data. Use separate held-out cases for a generalization check.

questions.prompt: A retrieved PDF tells a tool to export secrets. May document text expand the authenticated user's permissions? Type yes or no.
questions.explanation: Documents are untrusted data. The application must enforce tool permissions even when the model follows a malicious instruction.

questions.prompt: A final reply refuses an export, but the trace shows the unauthorized export already executed. Did the end-to-end defense succeed? Type yes or no.
questions.explanation: A safe reply cannot undo an unsafe action. Test the tool boundary and trace, not only the final sentence.

questions.prompt: Which pyproject.toml table declares required runtime distributions? Type the table name, without brackets.
questions.explanation: Runtime dependencies are declared in the project table, under dependencies.

questions.prompt: An installed script returns 2 from main. What integer exit status does its wrapper use?
questions.explanation: The wrapper exits using the callable’s return value.

questions.prompt: Which standard-library module reads bundled package resources? Type its full module name.
questions.explanation: importlib.resources finds data through the package’s loader.

questions.prompt: Does a successful editable install alone prove the built wheel contains defaults.json? Type yes or no.
questions.explanation: An editable install can see source files that were omitted from the built artifact.

questions.prompt: Pinning only a direct dependency also pins every transitive dependency. Type yes or no.
questions.explanation: Transitive constraints can still resolve to different versions.

questions.prompt: What pip subcommand checks declared installed dependency requirements? Type one word.
questions.explanation: pip check reports broken declared version requirements.

questions.prompt: Which artifact is directly installable without rebuilding its Python sources: wheel or sdist?
questions.explanation: A wheel is the built installable distribution; an sdist is a source archive.

questions.prompt: Can a successful type check alone prove correct runtime totals? Type yes or no.
questions.explanation: Type checking cannot establish the numerical behavior of every implementation.

questions.prompt: Which timeout category bounds waiting for an available pooled connection: connect, read, write or pool?
questions.explanation: Pool timeout bounds waiting for a connection slot.

questions.prompt: Does MockTransport prove real DNS and TLS routing work? Type yes or no.
questions.explanation: MockTransport bypasses the actual network and provides deterministic responses.

concepts.title: HTTP chunks, record framing & byte limits

questions.prompt: A line limit is 1024 bytes and excludes LF. Is a valid line of exactly 1024 bytes allowed? Type yes or no.
questions.explanation: This contract rejects only values greater than the inclusive line limit.

questions.prompt: Does a transport chunk always contain exactly one complete JSON record? Type yes or no.
questions.explanation: It may contain partial records or several records.

questions.prompt: What exception attribute holds the explicit original cause from raise ... from exc?
questions.explanation: The __cause__ attribute retains the explicitly chained exception.

questions.prompt: Under this ingestion lab contract, how many GET attempts are made for a rejected 503 status? Type an integer.
questions.explanation: The contract sends one GET and performs no silent retries.

concepts.title: Offline failure tests & the ingestion package

questions.prompt: Should the CLI print its success summary before the last input record has been validated? Type yes or no.
questions.explanation: A later failure must prevent publishing a partial success report.

questions.prompt: Does passing 28 finite public tests certify every production behavior? Type yes or no.
questions.explanation: The tests cover a stated finite contract; review and deployment evidence are separate.

questions.prompt: Which function-building pattern gives each filter independent parameter bindings?
questions.explanation: A factory call creates a new enclosing scope.

questions.prompt: Does capturing a mutable list automatically deep-copy it? Answer yes or no.
questions.explanation: The closure still refers to the same list.

questions.prompt: Which punctuation marks preceding parameters as positional-only?
questions.explanation: The slash introduces the positional-only boundary.

questions.prompt: Which absence marker commonly avoids a shared default list?
questions.explanation: Allocate a fresh list inside when the argument is None.

questions.prompt: Which functools helper preserves a wrapper target’s metadata?
questions.explanation: Use @wraps(target) on the inner wrapper.

questions.prompt: Which statement re-raises the current exception without constructing a replacement?
questions.explanation: A bare raise inside the handler preserves the caught exception.

questions.prompt: Which default pytest fixture scope creates fresh state for each test?
questions.explanation: Function scope isolates test setup.

questions.prompt: Which statement separates fixture setup from teardown?
questions.explanation: Code after yield performs teardown; use finally for reliable release.

concepts.title: Test doubles & patching the lookup site

questions.prompt: Which pytest fixture temporarily patches attributes and restores them after a test?
questions.explanation: Monkeypatch scopes changes to the test.

questions.prompt: Should a contract test replace the very function whose behavior it is evaluating? Answer yes or no.
questions.explanation: Keep that behavior real and replace its external dependencies.

questions.prompt: Which pytest fixture captures emitted logging records?
questions.explanation: Caplog observes actual LogRecords, not just mock logger calls.

questions.prompt: Who owns global handler configuration: library or application?
questions.explanation: The application controls destinations and formatting.

concepts.title: Bounded regex rules & the policy lab

questions.prompt: Which re operation requires a match of the entire input?
questions.explanation: Search can find only a fragment; fullmatch checks the whole value.

questions.prompt: For this contract, is 60001 valid? Answer yes or no.
questions.explanation: It exceeds the inclusive maximum 60000 even though it has five digits.

questions.prompt: Which keyword waits for a coroutine’s result inside an async function?
questions.explanation: Await drives or waits for asynchronous work.

questions.prompt: Does calling an async function automatically schedule its body? Answer yes or no.
questions.explanation: The call creates a coroutine object; scheduling or awaiting is separate.

questions.prompt: Which asyncio context owns and awaits related tasks?
questions.explanation: Create related work through a TaskGroup.

questions.prompt: Which handler keyword handles matching leaves of an exception group?
questions.explanation: Except-star handles matching leaves while unmatched errors still propagate.

questions.prompt: Which task method requests cancellation?
questions.explanation: Call cancel, then await the task to observe shutdown.

questions.prompt: Should a caught CancelledError usually be propagated after cleanup? Answer yes or no.
questions.explanation: Structured shutdown relies on cancellation remaining visible.

questions.prompt: Which error does an expired asyncio.timeout produce outside its context?
questions.explanation: The timeout context converts its own cancellation on exit.

questions.prompt: Does an asyncio deadline forcibly stop arbitrary blocking Python code? Answer yes or no.
questions.explanation: The task must cooperate and reach waiting opportunities.

questions.prompt: Which positive Queue setting bounds pending items?
questions.explanation: Use a positive maxsize; zero is unbounded.

questions.prompt: Which queue method balances a successfully retrieved item?
questions.explanation: Call task_done once for each successful get, including a sentinel.

questions.prompt: Which contextlib helper awaits closing an owned async generator?
questions.explanation: Aclosing pairs an owned generator with awaited cleanup.

questions.prompt: Which statement enters an asynchronous resource context?
questions.explanation: Async with awaits context entry and exit.

questions.prompt: Which HTTPX client provides asynchronous network operations?
questions.explanation: Use and await AsyncClient on the existing loop.

questions.prompt: Does Content-Length alone prove the actual streamed body stays within a limit? Answer yes or no.
questions.explanation: Count actual processed raw bytes rather than trusting the header.

questions.prompt: Which asyncio primitive signals that a task reached an observed point?
questions.explanation: Events establish task ordering without guessed sleeps.

questions.prompt: May the lab return success after only some configured sources complete? Answer yes or no.
questions.explanation: Every source must finish and close before the batch report is returned.

questions.prompt: Under default lookup, can an instance dictionary entry override a data descriptor? Answer yes or no.
questions.explanation: A data descriptor has priority over the same-named instance entry.

questions.prompt: Which fallback method can run when ordinary attribute lookup raises AttributeError?
questions.explanation: The fallback can run even when a property raised AttributeError internally.

questions.prompt: Which descriptor callback receives the owner and attribute name during class creation?
questions.explanation: It can choose a per-field storage name.

questions.prompt: For an exact-int contract, should True be accepted just because isinstance(True, int) is true? Answer yes or no.
questions.explanation: bool inherits int, but this contract excludes it.

questions.prompt: Which class attribute exposes the method resolution order?
questions.explanation: It shows the class order used by inheritance lookup.

questions.prompt: Does super always mean the lexically named direct parent? Answer yes or no.
questions.explanation: It continues after the current class in the receiver’s MRO.

questions.prompt: A container has __len__ returning 0 and no __bool__. Write the result of bool(container).
questions.explanation: Without __bool__, a zero length makes the container false.

questions.prompt: Does a tuple automatically freeze mutable objects inside it? Answer yes or no.
questions.explanation: Container immutability is not recursive element immutability.

questions.prompt: What singleton should __eq__ return for an unsupported operand?
questions.explanation: It lets comparison dispatch try the other operand; it differs from NotImplementedError.

questions.prompt: Must unequal keys always have different hashes? Answer yes or no.
questions.explanation: Collisions are permitted and equality distinguishes candidates.

concepts.title: Object contracts & the feed snapshot lab

questions.prompt: A snapshot accepts at most 64 elements. How many observations are needed to detect an overflowing stream?
questions.explanation: The 65th establishes overflow; do not request a 66th.

questions.prompt: Should a function close an iterator that its contract explicitly borrows? Answer yes or no.
questions.explanation: Its caller retains cleanup ownership; document consumption on failure.

concepts.title: Generics & related input and output types

questions.prompt: Which traditional typing factory declares a reusable type variable?
questions.explanation: TypeVar records a static relationship; it does not validate values.

questions.prompt: Does a type parameter automatically convert a runtime integer to text? Answer yes or no.
questions.explanation: It describes the relationship between types without converting the object.

questions.prompt: What variance describes a read-only producer of Dogs usable by readers expecting Animals?
questions.explanation: The producer can return the more specific compatible values.

questions.prompt: Is a writable list[Dog] safely assignable to a writable list[Animal]? Answer yes or no.
questions.explanation: The animal caller could append a value that is not a Dog.
